newsitem.title: USA: Goodyear earnings up on higher tire sales.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear earnings up on higher tire sales.

text.p: Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co. said Monday that higher tire sales helped drive an 8.1 percent increase in third quarter profits.
The Akron-based company said net income for the period was $170.2 million, or $1.09 per share, compared with $157.5 million and $1.03 per share in the same period last year.
The results were exactly in line with Wall Street analysts' expectations.
"Goodyear's worldwide tire unit sales during the quarter increased 6.1 percent over 1995, led by strong performances in Europe, Latin America and Asia," Goodyear Chairman Samir Gibara said.
"Our results were led by Goodyear operations in Europe and Latin America and also reflect lower raw material prices," Gibara added.

The company said revenues were hurt by lower sales of original equipment tires in North America, competitive pricing pressures in the North American replacement market, and the strengthening of the U.S. dollar.
Goodyear's stock was up $1.125 to $46.625 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
